AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase - creature creation IS construction - so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (corpse_slug.py:40-42). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set - the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:55-73 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none can fire, and sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks; (b) HP-roll inversion - the sim applies the power before the parity Niche roll (combat.py:267-268) and the game after it, but of the constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower reads max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:2063-2067), never at apply time, and RavenousPower 4 (CorpseSlug.cs:51,88 - GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 5, 4), non-ascension value LAST) is a flat constant; (c) roll ordering - CorpseSlug is the batch's one MachineMonster, so MachineMonster.__init__ DOES roll (state_machine.py:301) before the subclass applies the power - but every one of its three possible initial states is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's sticky early return fires and the roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Executed rather than assumed: `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b02.py seq` drives all three starter indices for 40 turns and reports 0 MonsterAi draws on both the reference machine and the port. All cited files are carried in this record's extra_sources. NOTE (tooling defect this batch found): `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py ctor-order` does NOT list this unit. Its `_CTOR` regex (the `_CTOR` regex in audit/tools/monster_probes.py, which this pipeline deliberately never hashes) is `def __init__\(self`, which cannot match a port whose signature wraps as `def __init__(<newline> self,`. Reproduce with `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b02.py ctor-regex`: the real population is 46, not the 35 SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 reports, and 11 units are missing from that list.

guards.what: Where StarterMoveIdx comes from. The game calls `CorpseSlug.EnsureCorpseSlugsStartWithDifferentMoves(models, base.Rng)` (CorpseSlugsNormal.cs:32, CorpseSlugsWeak.cs:32), and the helper draws `rng.NextInt(3)` off the PER-ENCOUNTER selection Rng (CorpseSlug.cs:135-144; EncounterModel.cs:49,268 is the stream, reproduced by rng.py:52-67's make_encounter_rng). The sim's CorpseSlugsEncounter.create_monsters (corpse_slug.py:79-84) ignores its `selection_rng` parameter entirely and draws `rng.randrange(3)` off the combat rng.
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-28: CorpseSlugsEncounter.create_monsters (corpse_slug.py:79-91) now CONSUMES its `selection_rng` -- `start = selection_rng.next_int(3)` -- reproducing CorpseSlugs{Normal,Weak}.cs:32 -> CorpseSlug.EnsureCorpseSlugsStartWithDifferentMoves (CorpseSlug.cs:135-144) drawing NextInt(3) off the per-encounter Rng, and run.py:1702-1706 builds that stream with rng.make_encounter_rng(seed, total_floor, encounter.entry) exactly as EncounterModel.cs:258-263 seeds it. Executed: `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b02.py enc-rng` now reports corpse_slugs_normal and corpse_slugs_weak consuming 1 selection draw against the game's 1 (they consumed 0 before), and the +1-per-slug stagger was already faithful. WAS: the parameter was ignored and the index came off the shared, unseeded combat random.Random, so every slug opened on the wrong move and a replay was not even run-to-run stable. Legacy (no rng_set) runs still fall back to the shared rng at corpse_slug.py:87 -- by construction, since a legacy run has no run seed to derive a per-encounter Rng from.
